Flood Insurance Data

Methodology

Sources

  • NFIP Redacted Policies v3 and Claims v3 — OpenFEMA API (keyless). Cost, full-risk premium, zones, claims.
  • Community Status Book v1 — OpenFEMA. CRS class and premium discount by community.
  • Disaster Declarations Summaries v2 — OpenFEMA. Federal flood/storm declarations.
  • Housing Assistance (Owners) v2 — OpenFEMA. FEMA aid paid to owners after disasters.
  • National Risk Index (counties) — FEMA ArcGIS (FEMA_NationalRiskIndex). Flood expected annual loss + percentile.
  • U.S. Census ACS 5-year (B25001) — U.S. Census Bureau API. Housing units, for the take-up ratio (policies per 100 homes).
  • Repetitive-Loss Flood Properties — OpenFEMA (Individual Assistance Multiple-Loss). FEMA-designated RL/SRL properties with more than one flood loss, per county.
  • NFIP Residential Penetration Rates — OpenFEMA. Share of residential structures with an NFIP policy, overall and inside the high-risk zone, per county.
  • NOAA NCEI Storm Events — NOAA. Recorded flood/flash-flood/coastal-flood events + NWS property-damage estimates, per county (1996 on).
  • Official Policy Information by State and Community workbook — reconciliation benchmark (a cross-check, not a dataset).

Ten federal datasets in all; the full-risk premium is a field within Policies and the PIF workbook is a reconciliation benchmark, not separate fetches.

Definitions & rules

  • Policy units = sum of policyCount, never a row count — condo-association records carry more than one unit.
  • Cost cohort: single-family primary-residence policies (occupancy 1/11, primary residence), annual cost = premium + fees.
  • Percentiles p25/p50/p75/p90 by inclusive interpolation.
  • Full-risk gap: share of cohort whose premium charged (totalInsurancePremiumOfThePolicy) is below FEMA's full-risk premium (fullRiskPremium); both are premium-only. The cost figures elsewhere use policyCost, which FEMA defines as premium plus the reserve fund assessment, federal policy fee and HFIAA surcharge, so they are not compared with full-risk.
  • Claims per 100: cumulative paid claims since 1978 over current policy units — a historical tally, not an annual rate or a flood probability.
  • Suppression: cost charts need ≥100 cohort policies; a ZIP page exists only if it passes the 3-part publish test (sufficiency, decision-relevant difference, distinct intent).
  • Dates: each figure shows its effective date and retrieval date; policy snapshot differs from other datasets' retrieval dates.

What the data cannot tell you

  • Your own premium (depends on elevation, coverage, deductible).
  • Private (non-NFIP) prices.
  • Your address's exact flood zone — use FEMA's Flood Map Service Center.
  • Why premiums are rising.
